outputs.en: The new study, published in the Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society, provides the first detailed description of soft tissues preserved in Montsecosuchus depereti, a Lower Cretaceous crocodylomorph discovered at the Pedrera de Meià site in the province of Lleida (Catalonia, Spain). By examining the fossil under ultraviolet light, researchers uncovered new evidence about its skin, sensory structures, respiratory anatomy, and possible color pattern. The work was led by the Institut Català de Paleontologia Miquel Crusafont.
outputs.zh: 这份新研究刊登在林南协会《动物学期刊》上,首次详细描述了在Lleida省(西班牙卡塔洛尼亚)Pedrera de Mei&agrave场址发现的低临界细胞囊形菌depereti保存的软组织,通过检查紫外线光下的化石,研究人员发现了有关其皮肤、感官结构、呼吸解剖和可能颜色形态的新证据,这项工作由Catal&agrave研究所领导,并得到了Paleontologia Miquel Crusafont的引导。

outputs.en: Approximately 125 million years ago, a small crocodile died in a karstic lake close to the coast of what is now the Catalan Pre-Pyrenees. Its body settled into fine lake sediments, where unusually favorable conditions helped preserve it in exceptional detail. Over time, those sediments became the lithographic limestones of the Pedrera de Meià, now part of the UNESCO Orígens Global Geopark.
outputs.zh: 大约1.25亿年前,一个小鳄鱼死在离现在的加泰罗尼亚先河沿岸附近的一个喀斯特湖中,它的身体沉积在湖中,那里异常有利的条件帮助它保存了非常详细的沉积物。随着时间的推移,这些沉积物成为了梅加格拉夫河的石灰岩;现在,它已成为教科文组织Orígens Global Geopark的一部分。

outputs.en: The breakthrough came while paleontologists Oscar Castillo and Jesús Serrano were building a database of fossils from the lithographic limestones of Montsec held in Catalan and European museums. When they examined the holotype of Montsecosuchus depereti under ultraviolet light, they noticed structures that appeared to be remnants of soft tissue.
outputs.zh: 突破的到来,正是古生物学家奥斯卡·卡斯蒂略和杰斯·加卢特;塞拉诺正在建立来自卡泰罗尼亚和欧洲博物馆的蒙特斯古石的石灰岩岩的化石数据库。 当他们检查紫外光下的蒙塞科苏斯·德佩雷蒂的原型时,他们注意到了似乎是软组织残余的结构。

outputs.en: Ultraviolet light can cause fossilized tissues and the surrounding rock to respond differently, making otherwise invisible structures stand out.
outputs.zh: 紫外光光可能会导致化石化组织和周围岩石的反应不同,使否则看不见的结构显得突出。

outputs.en: Using this technique, the team documented several kinds of soft tissue, including epidermal scales. Although Montsecosuchus depereti has been known to science since the early 20th century, the new analysis provides the first detailed picture of what its skin looked like.
outputs.zh: 使用这一技术,小组记录了几种软组织,包括上皮缩皮。 尽管自20世纪初以来,科学就一直了解蒙塞科苏古斯·德佩雷蒂,但新分析首次提供了其皮肤的详情。

outputs.en: The scales varied considerably in shape and size across different parts of the body. The researchers also found that the animal lacked the high caudal fin seen in modern crocodiles.
outputs.zh: 研究者还发现动物缺乏现代鳄鱼所看到的高鳍。

outputs.en: In living crocodiles, similar sensory organs can detect touch and changes in water pressure, while also responding to temperature and chemical signals. In Montsecosuchus, these possible sensory structures appear only in small scales located around the edges of the body. That distribution could suggest that such organs first evolved in specific localized areas before becoming more widespread across the skin in later crocodylomorph lineages.
outputs.zh: 在活鳄鱼体内,类似的感官器官可以探测水压的触摸和变化,同时对温度和化学信号作出反应。 在蒙塞科苏斯,这些可能的感官结构只在身体边缘的小型范围内出现。这种分布可能表明,这些器官首先在特定局部地区发展,然后在后来的长长长的长长长长长的长长长长的长长长的长长长的长长长的长长长的长长的长长的长长的长的长长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的长的短的长的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的短的

outputs.en: The ultraviolet analysis also exposed cartilaginous structures in the chest. These features indicate that Montsecosuchus already possessed an efficient respiratory system that shared certain similarities with those of modern crocodiles.
outputs.zh: 紫外线分析还暴露了胸腔的骨架结构,这些特征表明,Montsecuchus已经拥有一个与现代鳄鱼有某些相似之处的有效呼吸系统。

outputs.en: "These traits indicate that, despite being a primitive animal, it was already very well adapted to a semi-aquatic lifestyle," concludes Castillo-Visa.
outputs.zh: 并让这些动物适应半水生生活方式, 并得出Castillo-Visa的结论。

outputs.en: Perhaps the most striking discovery involves the animal's tail.
outputs.zh: 也许最惊人的发现 涉及动物的尾巴

outputs.en: Under ultraviolet light, some scales in the caudal region show alternating light and dark bands running across the tail. Researchers interpret these bands as possible evidence of the animal's original coloration.
outputs.zh: 在紫外线光下,在圆形区域的一些比例显示,光和暗带交替穿过尾巴。研究人员将这些带子解释为动物原始颜色的可能证据。

outputs.en: Scientists cannot yet determine the exact colors that produced the pattern.
outputs.zh: 科学家还无法确定产生这种图案的确切颜色。

outputs.en: "At the moment we cannot say for sure what color the crocodile's tail was, but it would be expected that it was not so different from current species, which also show different coloration patterns," explains Albert G. Sellés, co-author of the article.
outputs.zh: ”我们无法肯定鳄鱼尾巴的颜色, 但预计它与当前物种没有太大不同, 也显示出不同的颜色模式。 Albert G. Sellés, 文章的共同作者。

outputs.en: In addition to Oscar Castillo-Visa and Albert G. Sellés, Àngel Galobart (Institut Català de Paleontologia Miquel Crusafont and director of the Conca-Dellà Museum) and Phil Bell from the University of New England participated in the research.
outputs.zh: 除了奥斯卡·卡斯蒂略-维斯和阿尔伯特·G·塞勒和埃克·埃克特;s, e-Agrave;ngel Galobart(Catal&agrave研究所;Paleontologia Miquel Crusafont和Conca-Dell&agrave博物馆主任)和来自新英格兰大学的菲尔·贝尔参加了研究。

outputs.en: The research has been mainly funded by the VEBPI, PLEC2021-007903, and ARQ001SOL-173-2022 projects, with support from the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities, the NextGenerationEU/PRTR program, the Department of Culture of the Generalitat de Catalunya, and the CERCA program.
outputs.zh: 研究主要由VEBPI、PLEC2121-007903和ARQ001SOL-173-2022项目资助,并得到科学、创新和大学部、下一个GenerationEU/PRTR方案、加泰罗尼亚总工会文化司以及CERCA方案的支助。

outputs.en: The Pedrera de Meià is considered a Konservat-Lagerstätte, a term used for fossil sites with extraordinary preservation. At such locations, fossils may retain not only bones and other hard tissues, but also delicate soft structures that are usually lost during fossilization.
outputs.zh: 化石可以保留骨骼和其他硬组织,也可以保留化化过程中通常丢失的软软结构。

outputs.en: That exceptional preservation has made Pedrera de Meià an important site for studying Lower Cretaceous fish, amphibians, reptiles, and plants. More than 8,000 fossil specimens have been recovered there so far.
outputs.zh: 这一特殊保护使得Pedrera de Mei&agrave成为研究下克里泰鱼类、两栖动物、爬行动物和植物的重要场所。 到目前为止,已经在那里回收了8000多颗化石样本。 而在研究中,人们发现,这些样本的样本数量已经超过8000个。

outputs.en: The fossil record includes spiders, flies, wasps or beetles, insect larvae, crustaceans, vertebrates such as fish and amphibians, and a remarkable diversity of plants. Among them is Montsechia, the first known angiosperm in the world. The center is also part of the "Dinosaurs of the Pyrenees" project, a network of museums and interpretation centers showcasing the rich paleontological record of the Catalan Pyrenees.
outputs.zh: 化石记录包括蜘蛛、苍蝇、黄蜂或甲虫、幼虫、甲壳虫、脊椎动物(如鱼类和两栖动物)以及各种植物,其中莫名其妙的植物有:世界首个已知血管动物蒙特塞西亚。中心也是“比利牛斯人恐龙”项目的一部分,这是一个博物馆和口译中心网络,展示了卡泰罗尼亚比利牛的丰富古生物学记录。

outputs.en: Materials provided by Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
outputs.zh: 东京大学工业科学研究所提供的材料,注:内容可按风格和长度编辑。

outputs.en: A century ago, the Pan-American road promised a new era of fraternity between the two continents. Did it succeed?
outputs.zh: 一百年前,泛美道路承诺在两大洲之间开创一个兄弟情谊的新时代,它成功了吗?

outputs.en: Leônidas Borges de Oliveira drove the first 300 miles of the world’s longest road trip alone. The date of his departure, in early 1928, meant that the young Brazilian army officer also had the road almost entirely to himself. This gave him time to think about what he had taken on. The vehicle beneath him, a donated Ford Model T with a decade of delivering newspapers on the odometer, chattered with ease over alternating segments of fresh gravel and steaming asphalt that constituted Brazil’s new highway, connecting Rio de Janeiro with São Paulo. On both sides of the road, Oliveira surveyed the deforested Paraíba Valley, which had hosted the world’s first coffee boom – ranks of bean-fruiting bushes whose product had reached global markets in 60-kilo sacks on the backs of mules. Oliveira was among the first to see his nation at highway speed, and velocity could make the eroded landscapes of the past feel irrelevant. He believed he was chasing the future.
outputs.zh: 仅是998年初,他离开的那一天意味着巴西年轻军官也几乎完全拥有这条道路。 这给了他时间去思考他所走过的。 他下面的一辆汽车,捐赠的福特T型车,在水深计上投递了十年报纸,对巴西新高速公路巴西新公路中交替的新鲜碎石和蒸汽沥青进行轻松的交谈,这块石头和沥青是巴西的新高速公路,连接里约热内卢和圣保罗。 奥利维拉在公路两侧都勘察了被砍伐的帕拉伊巴谷,这块森林是全世界第一个咖啡繁荣的豆芽灌木,其产品在驴背面60公斤的袋中进入全球市场。 奥利维拉是最早看到巴西高速高速高速高速高速的国民之一,快速的过去风景可能让人感到不相干。 他认为他正在追逐着未来。

outputs.en: His compatriots shared his optimism. With shining medals around his neck and a new Swiss chronograph on his wrist, Oliveira departed from Rio to the fanfare of two brass bands and a flourish of civic oratory. He arrived in São Paulo to cheering crowds and a press corps keen to follow his automotive exploits. Oliveira’s rapid progress on this first leg, not to mention his countrymen’s enthusiastic support, fortified his resolve to push on to his final destination: the United States’ capital at Washington, DC.
outputs.zh: 他的同胞们分享了他的乐观。 Oliveira领着闪亮的奖牌,手腕上又贴了瑞士的记事表,从里约出发,来到了两个铜乐队的风光和民间歌舞厅的蓬勃发展。 他来到圣保罗,为人群欢呼,并派出一个热衷于跟踪汽车开发的记者团。 奥利维拉在第一腿上,更不用提他的同胞的热情支持,迅速进步,加强了他将最终目的地 — — 美国首都华盛顿 — — 推向他最后目的地的决心。

outputs.en: Oliveira’s inspiration to make the long drive sprang from a novel idea, first proposed in 1923: the construction of an automotive highway that would link up the Western Hemisphere with a long ribbon of asphalt. Nobody knew exactly where the proposal had originated, and some official reactions in Latin America were tepid, but the popular response revealed an accelerating enthusiasm, and auto makers moved to capitalise on it. In 1924, the US Department of Commerce, which was headed by former auto executives, welcomed delegates from 19 Latin American nations to the largest promotional junket the US had organised to date, including a greeting at the White House by President Calvin Coolidge and a month-long highway tour that circled from New York to North Carolina and Minnesota to Michigan. The objective was to promote what Americans were calling a ‘Highway of Friendship’ – a Pan-American road, from the northern reaches of Alaska to the tip of Tierra del Fuego, over which they hoped to see unfettered automotive travel and the emergence of stronger hemispheric cultural bonds.
outputs.zh: Oliveira的灵感是让这一长途车轮从1923年首次提出的新理念中激发出。 建造汽车高速公路,将西半球连接起来,长长的沥青丝带。 没有人确切知道提案的起源,拉丁美洲官方的反应也很迟缓,但民众的反应表明,人们的热情正在加速,汽车制造商也开始资本化。 1924年,美国商务部(前汽车经理)由前汽车经理领导,欢迎19个拉丁美洲国家的代表来到美国迄今组织的最大宣传小车,包括卡尔文·库利耶特总统在白宫的问候以及从纽约到北卡罗来纳州和明尼苏达到密歇根州长达一个月的公路巡航。 其目的是宣传美国人所谓的“友谊高速公路”泛美道路,从阿拉斯加北部到提拉德尔弗埃戈的顶端,他们希望看到汽车不受约束的交通和西半球文化纽带的出现。

outputs.en: What Oliveira ultimately wanted was an authentic Pan-American Union, two continents without passports, without customs, and without official barriers at the hemispheres’ many successive borders. Nearly a century later, the fraternal ideals that underpinned this dream and gave birth to the Pan-American Highway might appear unimaginably distant, subverted by nativist sentiment – but, in fact, remain alive in one of the two continents the road was supposed to link.
outputs.zh: 奥利维拉最终想要的是一个真正的泛美联盟,两个大陆没有护照,没有海关,也没有在半球的许多接连边界上的官方壁垒。 近一个世纪后,支撑这一梦想并诞生泛美高速公路的兄弟理想可能看起来不可想象地遥远,被民族主义情绪破坏,事实上,这条道路应该连接在两大大陆之一,但事实上,这条道路应该仍然能够活在其中的大陆中。

outputs.en: First, Oliveira had to prove it could be done. A few dozen had tried to reach the US before him. In fact, the first to road-test potential routes for such a highway were not American drivers in new American cars but Argentines and Brazilians piloting either luxury European sedans entirely inappropriate to the terrain or topless American jalopies of dubious reliability. Nobody had succeeded in – or even committed to, as Oliveira had – driving the entire expedition without a detour, that is, on the actual ground without placing one’s vehicle on the afterdeck of a ship or on a railroad flatcar to surpass a series of known, impenetrable topographies. Everyone told him, and kept telling him all along his route, that what he proposed was impossible. Brazilian highway officials doubted he would get out of Brazil.
outputs.zh: 首先,奥利维拉必须证明它能够做到这一点。 几十人试图在他之前就试图到达美国。 事实上,首先测试公路可能通往这条高速公路的路线的不是美国新汽车司机,而是阿根廷和巴西驾驶的豪华欧洲轿车完全不适合地形或令人怀疑的美国无足轻重的破天荒。 没有人成功或承诺过,因为奥利维拉没有绕路就驾驶了整个远征,也就是说,在实际地面上,没有将车放在船只的后甲上或铁路平板车上,以超过一系列已知的、不可渗透的地形。 所有人都告诉他,并一直告诉他,他的建议是不可能的。 巴西高速公路官员怀疑他会离开巴西。

outputs.en: Oliveira’s convictions kept him and two later companions at their task, plodding north, year after year. At every opportunity, he spoke with energy about the dreams surrounding the construction of a highway connecting the continents, of an imminent hemispheric fraternity, and his remarks were published approvingly in papers in every nation he passed through. At his arrival in Washington, however, US officials insisted that what he claimed to have done was impossible. Most were considerate enough not to say it to his face, and he had the honour of meeting President Franklin Roosevelt and speaking to a large audience at the Pan-American Union building. But almost nobody believed Oliveira’s claims. Engineers from the US Bureau of Public Roads had struggled to walk segments of the route, let alone motor along it. And they rejected his maps, which they described as not inaccurate but belated. The Americans had already projected the official route through spaces their surveyors had not yet dared to go.
outputs.zh: 奥利维拉的定罪使他和两个后来的同伴无法完成他们的任务,年复一年地向北倾斜。 他利用每一次机会,都满怀热情地谈论了围绕连接各大陆的高速公路的修建梦想,即即将到来的半球兄弟会,他的讲话在经过的每个国家都以论文中得到了认可。 但是,在他抵达华盛顿时,美国官员坚持认为他所说的不可能做到。 大多数人都心怀同情,不敢当面说,他有幸会见了总统富兰克林·罗斯福,并在泛美联盟大楼的广大观众。 但几乎没有人相信奥利维拉的主张。 美国公共道路局的工程师们在路段上挣扎着,更不用说沿着路的发动机了。 他们拒绝了他的地图,他们称之为不准确但已经过时了。 美国人已经通过空间规划了官方路线,他们的勘测员还没有敢于去。

outputs.en: Where the road ran out, his men disassembled their vehicles, packed the components onto mules, and marched them on foot
outputs.zh: 路路路路路路路路路路路路路路路途过,他手下拆卸了车辆,将部件装在骡子上,徒步行走,

outputs.en: Oliveira and his team with Augusto Sandino. From the book O Brasil através das três Américas by José Roberto Faraco Braga
outputs.zh: Oliveira及其团队与Augusto Sandino。来自何塞·罗伯托·法拉科·布拉加的《巴西的亚斯特雷斯·特拉维斯·德·德·美洲》一书。

outputs.en: In truth, Oliveira didn’t literally drive on four tyres over the entire route, though he cut no geographic corners. Where the road ran out or became too steep or narrow, his men disassembled their vehicles (he now had two Model Ts), packed the components onto mules, like sacks of coffee, and marched them on foot until the terrain again became drivable. As further proof, every step of the way, Oliveira’s maps detailed his progress, and he gifted copies of his charts to any state or national government that would receive them.
outputs.zh: 事实上,奥利维拉并没有在整个路线上开四个轮胎,尽管他没有切开任何地理角。 在道路已经开通或者太陡峭或者太窄的地方,他的手下拆卸了他们的车辆(他现在有两个模型Ts ), 将部件装在骡子上,比如一袋咖啡,并徒步行走,直到地形再次开通。 进一步证明,路的每一个步骤,奥利维拉的地图都详细描述了他的进度,并将他的图表副本赠送给任何接收他们的州或国家政府。

outputs.en: The Pan-American Highway that Oliveira hoped to pioneer was indeed born in a burst of fraternal rhetoric. Officially, however, the road was never just about driving a car from Patagonia to Alaska, or vice versa, for the mere amusement of tourists. It was to be a modern network connecting every national capital, from Ottawa and Washington to Santiago and Buenos Aires. And this was to be only a beginning. The network was to then expand until it reached every province and shore, facilitating trade and resource extraction, breaking down old stereotypes and softening contested borders in friendly cultural exchanges. The ideals remained potent for half a century, and in 1966 the US declared the entire US interstate system part of the Pan-American Highway network.
outputs.zh: 奥利维拉希望开创的泛美高速公路确实诞生于一连串兄弟般的言论中。 然而,官方说来,这条道路从来不仅仅是从帕塔哥尼亚开车到阿拉斯加,或者说相反,只是为游客的娱乐。 它应该是一个连接从渥太华和华盛顿到圣地亚哥和布宜诺斯艾利斯的每一个国家首都的现代化网络。 而这只是个开始。 网络要扩展到到达每一个省和海岸,便利贸易和资源开采,打破旧的陈规旧习,在友好的文化交流中软化有争议的边界。 理想在半个世纪里依然很强劲,1966年美国宣布泛美公路网是美国跨州系统的一部分。

outputs.en: In a strictly material sense, this greater project has been a remarkable success, millions of miles of functional automobile paths that have revolutionised movement and left few spaces inaccessible to wheels. By 1915, the US paved a road from Canada to Mexico. In 1917, Peru pushed its first highway into the Amazon Basin. Already by 1925, Venezuelans could drive over the Andes in comfort, and from 1931 Cubans could motor the full length of their island. The US built a primitive road across Canada to Alaska in 1942, during the war, and Mexican contractors reached Guatemala in 1950. The overall progress was extraordinary. Ironically, however, the key link in the system through Central America, over which the US took control and about which there was incomparable publicity, was the slowest to advance. Not till 1962 did the US-built highway reach Panama City. And not far beyond the Panama Canal, the road came to a sudden halt at the boundary of an almost mythical space between Panama and Colombia known from 1955 as the Darién Gap. Since about 1980, not a single mile of progress has been made to close it.
outputs.zh: 从严格物质意义上来说,这个更大的项目取得了显著的成功,数百万英里的汽车运行道路使运动发生了革命,使几乎没有车轮空间。 1915年,美国铺平了一条从加拿大到墨西哥的公路。 1917年,秘鲁将第一个公路推入亚马逊盆地。 早在1925年,委内瑞拉就可以在安第斯山脉上开进舒适车,从1931年,古巴可以满岛的汽车。 美国在战争期间于1942年修建了一条穿过加拿大到阿拉斯加的原始公路,墨西哥承包商于1950年抵达危地马拉。 总体进展是非同寻常的。 但是,具有讽刺意味的是,美国控制并有相当不相容的宣传的中美洲系统的关键连接是最缓慢的。 直到1962年,美国建造的高速公路才到达巴拿马城。 巴拿马运河之后,这条公路突然停在巴拿马和哥伦比亚之间一个几乎神秘的空间的边界上,而1955年被称为达林谷。 1980年前后,没有取得一英里的进展。

outputs.en: And just as Oliveira’s trip did not end in increased American brotherhood, the Pan-American Highway would harden national borders almost everywhere it went, rather than open them. If getting from one border to the next became increasingly easy, at the borders themselves, the road’s arrival threw up political, cultural and material barriers – walls, fences and even the Darién Gap itself, which at first was a geographical barrier universally condemned. By the late-1970s, the Gap came to be embraced as a permanent fixture by Panamanian officials, US diplomats and international environmentalists. The best current explanation for the highway’s unfinished status, the reason that Panama and Colombia are the only two bordering nations on Earth without an automotive connection of even the most rudimentary kind, is that Panama refuses to build a road they believe would serve as a superhighway for Colombian immigrants. The Gap is their border wall.
outputs.zh: 欧利维拉的行程并没有以美国兄弟情谊的增加而告终,泛美高速公路几乎会使几乎所有边境都硬化,而不是打开。 如果从一条边界到另一条边界越来越容易,那么在边界本身,公路的到来就掀起了政治、文化和物质壁垒—墙、围栏甚至达里安盖,这起初是被普遍谴责的地理壁垒。 到了20世纪70年代末,巴拿马官员、美国外交官和国际环境学家们将“盖”视为永久固定的。 目前对公路未完成状态的最佳解释,巴拿马和哥伦比亚是地球上唯一两个连通但连不到最简陋的汽车连接的邻国,其原因是巴拿马拒绝修建他们认为能成为哥伦比亚移民的高速公路。 盖普是他们的边境墙。

outputs.en: Popular attitudes toward immigrants had fluctuated with economic conditions but, for decades, flaring anti-immigrant sentiment had had little effect on general policy. True, the US barred the entry of prostitutes in 1875, convicts and the insane in 1882, and polygamists in 1891, but other than the 1882 blanket ban on Chinese nationals, most legislation had rather narrow targets against individuals defined as undesirables. Otherwise, the doors were mostly open. Policies, however, changed abruptly in the 1920s, and the highway’s promotion had some impact on the reversal. The same year that Coolidge spoke in favour of building the highway, he also declared that ‘America must be kept American,’ and US Congress passed the broadly restrictive Johnson-Reed Act, whose discriminatory quotas reduced immigrant arrivals by a harsh 80 per cent. Latin Americans were not included in the act, but already by 1929 the US began detaining and repatriating individuals of Mexican descent, some of whom had been born in the US.
outputs.zh: 人们对移民的公众态度随着经济状况而波动,但几十年来,反移民情绪的发酵对总体政策影响甚微。 诚然,美国禁止妓女入境的原因有1875年,罪犯和精神病患者在1885年,1882年,精神病患者在1882年,多子女者在1891年,但除了1882年全面禁止中国国民之外,大多数立法都针对被界定为不受欢迎的人,而目标则相当狭窄。 否则,大门大都敞开。 然而,20世纪20年代的政策发生了突然变化,公路的推进也影响了反弹。 酷利科赞成修建高速公路的同年,他也宣布“美国必须保留美国,”美国国会通过了限制广泛的强生里德法案,该法案的歧视性配额将移民抵达人数减少了80%。 拉美人没有被纳入法案,但到1929年美国就开始拘留和遣返墨西哥裔人,其中一些人出生于美国。

outputs.en: The barriers to migration were national, ethnic and racial, created to turn back the poor and car-less
outputs.zh: 移民的障碍是民族、族裔和种族的,这些障碍是用来扭转穷人和无汽车者的

outputs.en: Significantly, restrictions on entry did not apply to tourists. Nor to adventurers. At the time of Oliveira’s drive, one could still cross borders without being aware of them but, increasingly, legal admittance to a nation required both passports and visas, and the red tape could be thick. Still, Oliveira found no insurmountable official barriers to his expedition’s actual progress. Indeed, the best way to identify yourself as a safe holidaymaker, or a legitimate explorer – someone who posed little threat of overstaying one’s welcome – was to arrive at the border by car. The automobile signalled one’s status and, if passage by car was fast on the highway, entry was almost certain – if not quick and painless – once at the border.
outputs.zh: 重要的是,入境限制不适用于游客,也不适用于冒险家。 在奥利维拉的驾车时,人们仍然可以在不知情的情况下跨越边境,但越来越多的是,合法进入一个国家需要护照和签证,而繁文缛节的手续可能很繁琐。 尽管如此,奥利维拉没有发现任何无法逾越的官方障碍阻碍其探险队的实际进展。 事实上,自我定位为安全节假日操控者或对超额停留欢迎威胁很小的合法探险员的最佳方式就是乘车抵达边境。 汽车表明自己的身份,如果汽车在高速公路上快速通过,入境几乎是肯定的,如果不是快速和无痛的话,一次在边境。

outputs.en: So those who took to the road in their millions didn’t come in cars with sunglasses on their noses. Rather, they sought new homes far from the places of their chance births. The majority moved on foot from rural areas to the largest cities in their own nations, the great urban migration that began in the 1930s, explained in part by new industrial jobs but greatly facilitated by new roads. Others went greater distances to settle in neighbouring nations: Colombians to Panama City; Nicaraguans to San José; Paraguayans and Bolivians to Buenos Aires. The most adventurous made the long trip to the US. While the highway made movement overland for migrants on foot substantially easier, once they arrived at a border, they typically came up against formidable legal obstacles. Even if they had secured the proper papers, they might be rejected because, without cars, they were identified as poor migrants. The administrative barriers to migration were national, ethnic and racial in character but, most specifically, they were created to turn back the poor and car-less.
outputs.zh: 这些人在数百万人中走上了公路,但他们却没有坐着满鼻子太阳眼镜的汽车。 相反,他们寻找远离出生地点的新家。 大多数人从农村地区步行到本国最大的城市,从1930年代开始的大规模城市移民,部分是由于新的工业工作,但大为便利,新公路也大大促进了这种移民。 其他人则走远到邻国定居:哥伦比亚人到巴拿马城;尼加拉瓜人到圣何塞;尼加拉瓜人到圣何塞;巴拉圭人和玻利维亚人到布宜诺斯艾利斯。 最冒险的人到美国旅行很长。 虽然高速公路让移民步行旅行更加容易,但他们到达边境后通常会遇到巨大的法律障碍。 即使他们有适当的证件,他们也可能被拒绝,因为没有汽车,他们会被确认为贫穷移民。 移民的行政障碍是民族、种族和种族性质的,但最具体地说,他们被创建起来是为了让穷人和没有汽车的人回路。

outputs.en: Hence, migrants circumvented officials by crossing borders where there were no roads. Nicaraguans arrived within view of Costa Rica on chartered buses that left them on a lonely highway that paralleled the border. Under the cover of night, they walked into Costa Rica where another bus picked them up and dropped them in San José the same day. Migrants moving north through Guatemala avoided the Mexican immigration office on the bridge over the Suchiate River, crossing the same on rubber rafts for a small fee, often within sight of authorities. To get across the US border, there were dozens of ways to get around official barriers, most of them now facilitated by Mexican cartels.
outputs.zh: 因此,移民绕过没有道路的边境,绕过官员,尼加拉瓜人乘坐包租的公共汽车来到哥斯达黎加,乘坐的汽车使他们乘坐与边界平行的一条孤独高速公路。在夜间,他们走进哥斯达黎加,另一辆公共汽车接了他们,并于当天在圣何塞下车。移民在经过危地马拉的北边,避开了苏希亚特河桥上的墨西哥移民办事处,他们常常在当局的眼皮底下,在橡胶木筏上通过同样的地点,收取少量费用。为了跨越美国边境,有数十条途径绕过官方的路障,其中多数现在由墨西哥卡特尔协助。

outputs.en: Important elements of the highway’s original ideals have endured even in the face of the dominant, contrary trends in immigration policy. Strikingly, beginning in 2010, nations in South America that in the past had been at war, often over the very boundaries that separated them, states whose individuals still retain an often palpable dislike for one another, came together to agree that, for the purposes of immigration, their borders would essentially cease to exist. Agreements strove to recharacterise immigration as a solution rather than a problem: the free movement of people was likely to decrease national tensions, enhance labour allocation, and recognise migrants’ basic human dignity by eliminating discrimination in work, healthcare and civil rights. While the EU seemed to be suffering setbacks, such as the loss of the UK, South America quickly gained an almost universal adherence.
outputs.zh: 即便在移民政策中出现了占主导地位的相反趋势,高速公路最初理想的重要内容也依然在不断延续。 令人惊讶的是,从2010年开始,过去曾处于战争之中的南美国家,往往在隔离它们的国家的边界上,其个人仍然对彼此保持明显的厌恶,它们一致认为,为了移民的目的,它们的边界基本上将不复存在。 协议试图将移民重新定性为解决办法而不是问题:人民的自由行动有可能通过消除工作、保健和公民权利方面的歧视来缓解国家紧张局势,增加劳动力分配,承认移民的基本人格尊严。 欧盟似乎正在遭受挫折,比如英国的丧失,但南美却很快获得了几乎普遍的遵守。

outputs.en: In 1932, the Darién Gap was wider than it is today, and it was the only place that Oliveira was forced to backtrack. He attempted to drive it even though the Colombian military had told him it was impossible. Broad swamps and malarial fevers forced the Brazilians to place their disassembled Fords on the deck of a boat for the first and only time. Oliveira, who might be in the running for the most optimistic person to have ever lived, opined that the Pan-American Highway would never be built overland though the Gap. The topography, he believed, was just too difficult. On that point, he was wrong. Humans have built roads through, over, and under terrain far more difficult than the Gap: Mexico’s Durango to Mazatlán Highway conquers the Sierra Madre with 63 tunnels and 115 bridges, one of them 400 metres high; the Faroese have tunnelled 600 feet below the Atlantic Ocean to connect their remote islands, one segment of which includes the world’s first subseafloor roundabout.
outputs.zh: 1932年,达里安河谷比今天更加宽阔,也是奥利维拉被迫背弃道路的唯一地方。他试图开车开。 尽管哥伦比亚军方告诉他这是不可能的。 广面积的沼泽和疟疾热迫使巴西人第一次和唯一一次将拆卸的福特放在船上甲板上。 奥利维拉可能为最乐观的人跑步,他相信泛美公路不会通过河口在陆地上修建。 他认为,地形太困难了。 在这一点上,他错了。 人类在穿越、穿越和在地形下修建的道路比Gap要困难得多:墨西哥的杜兰戈至马扎特兰公路用63条隧道和115座桥梁征服了塞拉马德雷,其中一座高达400米;法罗索人已经从大西洋下方600英尺的隧道中挖出600英尺的隧道,连接他们边远的岛屿,其中一部分包括世界第一个海底环绕。

newline.zh: 两行句第一行。第二行继续同样的思路。
